newsitem.title: UK: Rugby union - Five Nations championship saved.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union - Five Nations championship saved.

text.p: The Five Nations rugby union championship has been saved "for the foreseeable future" following a last-ditch meeting between representatives of England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland, it was announced on Thursday.

Rugby Football Union treasurer Colin Herridge read out a statement agreed in the early hours of the morning stating that "an accord" had been reached saving the championship, which had been under threat following a row over television revenue.
The original dispute arose when England announced they had sold television rights covering their matches in the tournament, traditional centre-piece of the northern hemisphere season.
The other nations insisted any deal should be done collectively and rejected their shares of the 87.5 million stg contract the RFU had already signed with satellite television operator BSkyB.
The RFU still insist the BSkyB deal is legally binding and Herridge said the RFU was "very pleased" to have finally negotiated a compromise after months of failure.
The news will be greeted with relief everywhere and could pave the way to a swifter solution to a parallel row between the English union and their top clubs.

The national squad boycotted a scheduled training session on Wednesday, but RFU secretary Tony Hallett said he was hopeful a compromise could be reached before October 11, the date the clubs have indicated they will split from the RFU.
